title: Why It Was Almost Impossible to Make the Blue LED
beats: LED color is not the plastic; transparent LED glows red; color comes from electronics
Red 1962, green soon after, then decades of failure; blue would unlock white light
Introduce Nakamura at tiny Nichia, scavenged lab, told to quit; gets a 3M dollar gamble
Light bulbs are terrible: mostly infrared heat; LED primarily makes light
Energy levels as seats in a hockey stadium; atoms together form bands; valence vs conduction as balcony
Conductor, insulator, then semiconductor with small gap; holes as moving empty seats
Doping: phosphorus gives n-type, boron gives p-type, with donor/acceptor levels
Join p and n: diffusion, depletion region, forward bias shrinks it, electrons fall and emit photon
Band gap sets color; silicon infrared (remote control); blue needs larger gap, so hard
Three hurdles implicitly set: crystal quality, p-type, brightness (1000 microwatts)
MOCVD for clean crystal; Nakamura spends a year building a reactor in Florida
Two candidates: zinc selenide (safe, no p-type) vs gallium nitride (16% mismatch); Nakamura picks GaN for low competition
500 attendees at ZnSe talks vs 5 at GaN; Akasaki and Amano's AlN buffer layer
Daily 7am-7pm routine for 1.5 years; two-flow reactor with inert downward gas
Management orders stop; he crumples notes; publishes first paper (one down, four to go)
P-type GaN: electron beam worked for A&A, Nakamura tries just heat (annealing); hydrogen from ammonia plugs holes
Indium gallium nitride well via pumping as much indium as possible; electrons leak, so add AlGaN hill
Final structure far more complex than anyone imagined; 1500 microwatts, 450 nm
Commercial explosion; yellow phosphor makes white; compensation lawsuit, 170 dollar bonus
LED revolution, circadian blue light, 1.4 billion tons CO2; micro and UV LEDs
Nobel 2014, PhD and papers (the backup plan); blue as favorite color; skills conclusion

theory: Veritasium makes physics necessary by posing it as the obstacle in a human story, so the band-gap lecture arrives exactly when the viewer needs it to see why blue is hard. The three hurdles reuse the same story pattern, so the viewer learns the structure and can predict the next step.
velocity: Orchestrator: open physics blocks only after a concrete obstacle exists the learner cares about
Voice: use one persistent physical analogy (stadium seats) across several concepts, and break it where it stops working
Learner model: track which hurdle-like sub-goals have been solved to offer a roadmap view
Scene builder: depict band diagrams as seats that fill and move; animate hole motion
Evals: check that every new technical term is linked to the goal it serves
